title: Antidromic AV reentrant tachycardia
summary: The circuit runs the opposite way to orthodromic AVRT: down the accessory pathway, up the AV node. The QRS is wide.

events.label: Atrial activation
events.caption: The atria are activated, starting at the AV node end of the circuit.

events.label: Down the accessory pathway
events.caption: The impulse reaches the accessory pathway and crosses it to the ventricle without delay. The ventricle is activated from the pathway end, outside the normal conduction system.

events.label: Back up the His bundle
events.caption: The ventricular impulse then enters the His-Purkinje system backwards and climbs the AV node in reverse.
events.ecg: The QRS is wide because the ventricles are not activated by the normal system.

events.label: Tachycardia
events.caption: The circuit repeats at about 200 per minute: the reverse of orthodromic AVRT.
events.ecg: A regular wide-complex tachycardia, which can look like VT.

teaching_points: Antidromic AVRT: antegrade conduction down the accessory pathway and retrograde up the AV node, giving a wide QRS.
It is part of the differential diagnosis of wide-complex tachycardia.
It is much rarer than orthodromic AVRT.
